Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
<mga...@lego.hrz.uni-bielefeld.de> wrote:
>This is my question. If I have take a Vampire into my controlled Zone after
>stealing it with the graverobering cart, and the player who controlled this

>cart is ousted, what happens?...

When a player is ousted, all cards that players own are burned. So in this
case, the vampire you stole via Grave Robbing is burned.

Tom Wylie rec.games.trading-cards.* Network Representative for
aa...@cats.ucsc.edu Wizards of the Coast, Inc.

Unfortunately one of the Explicit rulings in Jyhad is that whenever a player
is ousted from the game every card he came to the table with goes with him/her
This is because I may get ousted in the first 30 minutes of the game and not
want/be able to hang around for the other 10 people to lose. So I leave with
all of my cards. It is not a good, logical ruling, however it makes meta-game
sense.

Hope this Helps.
Stu

A question along these lines came up when we were playing last
Saturday. I had called a vote for ``Rumors of Gehenna'' which
states that a set of Methuselahs gains the ability to play
two master cards during their turn. The card further states
that the card can be removed by a vote. The question we had
was whether the effect of the vote died with the card or
whether the vote was necessary to take away the benefit gained
by the earlier vote.

Can someone clear this point up for me?

Messages.Author: D.P. Hammersley
Messages.Body:
>A question along these lines came up when we were playing last
>Saturday. I had called a vote for ``Rumors of Gehenna'' which
>states that a set of Methuselahs gains the ability to play
>two master cards during their turn. The card further states
>that the card can be removed by a vote. The question we had
>was whether the effect of the vote died with the card or
>whether the vote was necessary to take away the benefit gained
>by the earlier vote.

>Can someone clear this point up for me?

The card itself isn't actually in play - only it is helpful to keep it around
to remind everyone of its effects.

The benefits can only be removed by a successful vote to counter the initial
vote.

Pete
